item.description: Ford Motor is recalling 148,663 vehicles in the U.S. due to a loss of driver power and loss of headlight function or windshield washing system function, which can reduce visibility, the U.S. Related: NHTSA: Some Older Ford Cars, SUVs Pose Unreasonable Safety Risks (Reporting by Gupta in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Apple Accuses OpenAI of Destroying Evidence in Exchange of Barbs
item.description: escalated its legal battle against OpenAI, claiming in a court filing that OpenAI is actively destroying crucial evidence and that former iPhone engineer Chang Liu “not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work” at the AI company. The laptop also contains evidence that Liu “sent instructions for destroying evidence to an OpenAI colleague who confirmed she would comply,” Apple’s lawyers said. Related: OpenAI Asks Judge to Toss Apple’s Trade Secrets Lawsuit According to Apple’s latest filing, OpenAI “only recently” provided a key piece of evidence: an Apple-issued MacBook that Liu had been using since departing the company.

item.title: TCL Sues Samsung for False Advertising Over ‘Mini LED’ Televisions
item.description: “Samsung’s false advertising misled consumers who wanted the higher picture quality associated with Mini LED televisions into buying Samsung’s falsely labeled product, unfairly damaging TCL’s sales, goodwill, and valuable technology in the process,” TCL attorney R.C. Chinese consumer electronics company TCL has sued South Korea’s Samsung in Los Angeles federal court, accusing its rival of falsely advertising some televisions as using “Mini LED” technology. TCL’s lawsuit said that the Mini LED technology in its televisions delivers “substantially better picture with greater dynamic range and higher contrast ratios.” The company said it overtook Samsung in U.S.

item.title: LaGuardia Air Traffic Controllers Left an Hour Early Before Deadly Crash
item.description: Two air traffic controllers could be fired for leaving the tower at New York’s LaGuardia Airport about an hour early on the night that an Air Canada jet smashed into a fire truck crossing the runway, killing both pilots, according to a government official familiar with the investigation. The FAA said in a statement that the agency “is committed to holding employees accountable, and we will not compromise the safety or efficiency of the national airspace system.” Transportation Secretary calls early departures timecard fraud Tom Lintner saw early departures repeatedly during his decades-long career at the FAA that included a stint as a LaGuardia controller before going on to oversee all air traffic control investigations, but he said it shouldn’t be allowed to continue. Because the two controllers left work early that night, there were only two people left in the tower to direct an unusual flurry of flights while dealing with an emergency on another plane on the ground.

item.title: Steep Declines in Child Restraint Use Prompt AAA Safety Reminder
item.description: New analysis of nationwide crash data finds that child safety seat and booster seat use declines sharply with age, starting when kids are just 3 years old, according to AAA. This steep decline in child restraint use is concerning because many children have not yet outgrown the need for a car seat or booster seat based on their size and development. Parents and caregivers can schedule a free visit with a certified Child Passenger Safety Technician in their area or online to make sure their child’s restraint system is right for their size and developmental needs.” Car crashes remain a leading cause of death for children.

item.title: Over $1M in Stolen Goods Recovered by CHP During Organized Retail Crime Crackdown
item.description: Participation in a recent National Organized Retail Crime Blitz, helped the California Highway Patrol recover $1.05 million in stolen goods. From August 1 through 9, the CHP Organized Retail Crime Task Force (ORCTF) saturated communities and led coordinated enforcement operations at several businesses, shopping centers and retail stores statewide, apprehending suspects involved in organized retail theft. In the first seven months of 2026, the CHP made nearly 350 retail theft arrests, investigated more than 280 incidents, and assisted partner agencies with more than 80 investigations, recovering an estimated $6.7 million in stolen goods.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Proptech Funding Holds Up, But Investors Are Placing Different Bets
item.description: While investors haven’t given up on proptech, funding to startups in the space remains down as interest rates hover in the 6% to 7% range . Venture funding to proptech startups is nowhere near its peak and still hasn’t returned to pre-pandemic levels, as higher interest rates make real estate a tougher place to invest, leading to fewer deals and raising the bar for startups seeking capital. But startup investors haven’t abandoned the sector, either, Crunchbase data shows.

item.title: SEADRIF makes over $1 million in payouts to Lao PDR and WFP under parametric policies
item.description: The Southeast Asia Disaster Risk Insurance Facility (SEADRIF Insurance Company) has made payouts of USD 1.14 million to the Government of Lao PDR and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), after heavy rainfall and widespread flooding triggered both Lao PDR’s two-year parametric sovereign policy and WFP’s 2026 disaster resilience policy. Prolonged southwest monsoon conditions and active low-pressure systems saw more than 260,000 people impacted by heavy rainfall and widespread flooding across Lao PDR, surpassing the 200,000-person mark reported by the Lao PDR National Disaster Management Office (NDMO), which triggered a first payout threshold under both SEADRIF policies. Following verification, SEADRIF paid out USD 1 million to the Government of Lao PDR, under its USD 8 million annual coverage, and USD 137,500 to WFP, under its USD 1.1 million policy.

item.title: Reinsurance sidecar market estimated at record $23bn in 2026: Aon Securities
item.description: The outstanding market for collateralized reinsurance sidecar structures has reached a new record high of $23 billion in 2026, representing roughly 50% growth since the end of 2024, according to estimates from Aon Securities. Aon Securities has been tracking the expansion of the reinsurance sidecar market over recent years. The reinsurance sidecar market then increased by a staggering 70%, reaching a new record high of $17 billion by the end of June 30th 2025 .

item.title: Marc Brogli rejoins Euler ILS Partners investment team
item.description: Euler ILS Partners, the specialist Swiss insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager, has confirmed that Marc Brogli has been appointed Investment Director after almost four years with Aon Securities. “Having previously been part of our team, Marc brings not only deep market expertise, a strong industry network, and a unique combination of buy-side and advisory experience, but also a thorough understanding of our investment platform, culture, and processes,” Euler ILS Partners commented on a LinkedIn post. Prior to Aon Securities, Brogli worked at Credit Suisse Insurance Linked Strategies Ltd., before the firm rebranded to Euler ILS Partners.

item.title: SRS Altitude approved as Lloyd’s Coverholder
item.description: Strategic Risk Solutions (SRS), an independent insurance company manager, has announced that SRS Altitude has been approved as a Lloyd’s Coverholder. Loredana Mazzoleni Neglén, CEO of SRS Altitude, said, “Becoming a Lloyd’s Coverholder is a significant milestone for SRS Altitude and strengthens our ability to deliver tailored alternative risk solutions backed by one of the world’s leading insurance markets.” Brady Young, CEO of Strategic Risk Solutions, added, “This achievement reflects the strength of the SRS Altitude platform and team, and further positions SRS to support the growing demand of clients for captive solutions in the Lloyd’s market.” SRS Altitude’s Coverholder approval, supported by strategic partner Beazley, enhances its ability to bring alternative risk solutions to corporate clients and captives globally.

item.title: Hannover Re US names Conrad as VP & Head of Traditional Life Pricing and Data Analytics
item.description: Hannover Life Reassurance Company of America (Hannover Re US) has appointed Sean Conrad as Vice President (VP) and Head of Traditional Life Pricing and Data Analytics, effective immediately. In his new role, Conrad’s remit within the traditional life solutions will include traditional pricing, data analytics, and accelerated underwriting. Over his tenure at the firm, Conrad has held several leadership roles spanning pricing, accelerated underwriting, digital distribution, mortality analytics, innovation, and strategic business development.

item.title: ‘Abundant capital should be a wake-up call, not a victory lap,’ says Rousseau, Marsh Re
item.description: “Abundant capital should be a wake-up call, not a victory lap. Reinsurance capital continues to build, creating a favourable environment for insurers but placing greater pressure on reinsurers to demonstrate the value they bring to clients, according to Laurent Rousseau, CEO of Global Capital & Advisory, and Europe and IMEA at Marsh Re. Speaking ahead of the Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous, Rousseau said the continued growth in capital was not simply a temporary feature of the market, but part of its longer-term structure.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: Coalition Launches Cyber Insurance for Large UK Enterprises
item.description: Coalition, the San Francisco-based cyber managing general agent and cyber-security firm, has launched Active Cyber Insurance for Enterprises in the UK, a solution designed to meet the complex cyber risk needs of large organizations. Following the announcement of Coalition’s expanded strategic relationship with Allianz Commercial , Coalition now offers up to £20 million in cyber limits to large businesses in the United Kingdom. “Our innovative enterprise solution reimagines cyber protection for the complex risks faced by global enterprises,” said Shawn Ram, Coalition’s chief revenue officer.

item.title: Texas Mobilizes Ahead of Tropical Storm Edouard
item.description: Texas is mobilizing emergency response crews in anticipation of expected flash flooding from a now fully-formed tropical storm that forecasters predicted would hit the southeast part of the state on Tuesday. Federal forecasters elevated a tropical depression in the Gulf of Mexico to Tropical Storm Edouard on Monday evening. A storm surge warning from High Island, Texas, to the Vermillion/Cameron Parish Line in Louisiana was also issued.

item.title: ‘Cockroaches in My Food’ Claim Leads to Insurance Fraud Charge
item.description: A Warren County, North Carolina man has been charged with insurance fraud for allegedly seeking an insurance payment from a restaurant where he claims he found cockroaches in his food. Special agents with the Department of Insurance Criminal Investigations Division have accused Jones of falsely reporting that he found two cockroaches in his food at a Creedmoor KFC. Jones was charged with one count of insurance fraud and one count of attempting to obtain property by false pretense.

item.title: $17bn deal: Aon acquires USI Insurance Services from KKR to target US middle market
item.description: The post $17bn deal: Aon acquires USI Insurance Services from KKR to target US middle market appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Aon has confirmed a definitive agreement to acquire USI Insurance Services from private equity firm KKR for $17bn. Aon said the deal bolsters its goal of targeting the US middle-market segment, building on its 2024 acquisition of NFP for $13bn.

item.title: ISC adds CFC cyber program to marketplace
item.description: ISC has partnered with CFC to offer standalone cyber coverage through its ISCx digital marketplace. The program offers first- and third-party coverage for businesses of all sizes, including ransomware, social engineering fraud, cyber extortion, business interruption, regulatory fines, legal defense and incident-response costs. Policyholders also receive cyber-risk tools, including phishing training, dark-web monitoring, vulnerability scanning, threat intelligence and incident-response planning.

item.title: Stack Health raises $21 million
item.description: Stack Health , a Columbus startup offering an alternative to group health insurance, has closed a $21 million seed round led by 8VC, with participation from A*, Heartland Ventures, The O.H.I.O. Founded by the founder and former CEO of Beam Benefits Alex Frommeyer, Stack uses individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements (ICHRAs) to help businesses set an insurance amount and reimburse health care spending. Stack then helps employees compare and select individual plans.

item.title: Huscarl raises $5.6 million for AI actuarial platform
item.description: Huscarl , a startup building AI tools for self-insured companies, captives and risk retention groups, has raised $5.6 million in seed funding led by FRST, with participation from Y Combinator and other Silicon Valley investors. The company’s platform ingests unstructured data, develops risk models for emerging or unusual exposures, and automates actuarial workflows. Huscarl offers one-off actuarial studies, appointed-actuary services for captives, and outsourced underwriting for group captives and risk retention groups.

item.title: Honda, Nissan Target Rollout of Joint Vehicle Software in 2029
item.description: Honda and Nissan said they aim to establish common specifications for core ECUs within their vehicles’ electrical and electronic architecture, as well as operating systems and parts of the middleware and vehicle-control software. Japanese automakers Nissan and Honda said on Monday they would jointly develop standardized electronic control units (ECUs) for software-defined vehicles (SDVs), deepening their collaboration on more advanced car technology. The companies plan to introduce an architecture incorporating the jointly developed ECUs and software in next-generation vehicles from the 2029 financial year onwards, they said in a joint statement.

item.title: Medical Chronology Software for Workers’ Comp: Features That Determine Defensibility
item.description: View Series Choosing medical chronology software for workers’ compensation goes beyond comparing turnaround times and feature lists. That shifts medical chronology software from being a document review tool to becoming part of a broader claims decision intelligence workflow that helps organizations improve consistency, reduce administrative effort, and make faster, better-informed decisions at scale. Different teams interact with the same medical chronology in very different ways.

item.title: OSINT & Background Investigations: A Practical Toolkit for Modern Claims Handling
item.description: OSINT and the background investigations it supports has quietly become one of the more important skills in the claims toolkit. OSINT touches nearly every corner of claims handling bodily injury and soft tissue claims, workers’ comp, property claims, SIU and liability investigations. But its role in background investigations deserves particular attention, because it’s often the piece that gets skipped when adjusters are moving fast.

item.title: FCA urges young adults to check for unclaimed Child Trust Funds
item.description: As students return to college and university this month, the FCA is urging young adults and parents to check whether they have a forgotten Child Trust Fund waiting to be claimed – potentially worth thousands of pounds. Figures from HMRC show that 760,000 matured Child Trust Funds, worth an average of £2,000 each, remain unclaimed. Some companies, including those advertising on social media, are offering to 'find' and claim Child Trust Funds on people's behalf – often for a hefty fee or a cut of the final payout.

item.title: ILS fund performance continues to rise in 2026, average July return hit 1.05%: ILS Advisers
item.description: The performance of insurance-linked securities investment fund strategies, across catastrophe bonds and private ILS, has continued to rise through July 2026 with the month delivering the best returns of the year so far for the asset class, as measured by the ILS Advisers Fund Index . This strong July average ILS fund return has lifted performance for the first seven months of 2026 to 5.12% for the Index. ILS Advisers said that, “Pure cat bond funds as a group posted a 0.95% gain for the month, while funds incorporating private ILS strategies were up by 1.23% on average.” The range of returns reported was also indicative of a very strong month for the ILS fund marketplace, as the worst performing fund delivered a 0.45% return and the best-performing a much stronger 2.88% for July 2026.

item.title: AM Best maintains stable outlook on ‘fundamentally strong’ global reinsurance segment
item.description: Global credit rating agency AM Best has maintained its stable outlook on the global non-life reinsurance segment, assessing that the market “remains fundamentally strong” despite clear softening in property, challenges in certain classes of casualty in the US, and an overall competitive landscape. Back in January, AM Best revised its global reinsurance sector outlook to stable from positive , driven by the accelerated softening of property reinsurance rates. Ahead of the annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo this week, the rating agency has maintained its stable sector outlook, based on numerous factors, including a pricing environment that is still supportive of solid operating results, strong nominal and risk-adjusted capital positions, sustained underwriting performance in property cat covers, and higher interest rates which bolster investment income for firms.

item.title: Alternative capital rose 9% in H1’26 to record $147bn: Gallagher Re
item.description: Global non-life alternative reinsurance capital increased by 9%, or USD 12 billion in the first half of 2026 to a record USD 147 billion, driven by favourable returns and net inflows of capital, as total reinsurance capital rose by 5% in the period to a high of USD 688 billion, according to reinsurance broker Gallagher Re. Both traditional and alternative reinsurance capital growth has been strong since 2023, with total dedicated capital rising from USD 547 billion at year-end 2023 to a record USD 688 billion at the end of June 2026. During this time, traditional capital increased by 23% to USD 541 billion, while alternative capital rose by more than 37% to the aforementioned USD 147 billion.

item.title: Tokio Marine HCC’s CPLG names Brian Alva as SVP of Underwriting
item.description: Cyber & Professional Lines Group (CPLG), part of the Tokio Marine HCC group of companies and headquartered in Houston, Texas, has appointed Brian Alva as Senior Vice President of Underwriting, where he will take responsibility for the group’s cyber and technology underwriting. We are excited to have Brian help shape the next chapter of CPLG’s cyber business.” Alva said: “Cyber risk continues to evolve at extraordinary speed, and the opportunity for CPLG is to combine underwriting excellence with the data, technology and services needed to stay ahead of that change.” He continued: “I am excited to join CPLG and return to an organisation I know well, working alongside a strong team to build on its deep specialty expertise, strengthen broker relationships and deliver thoughtful, sustainable solutions for cyber risk.” As part of his new role, Alva will oversee efforts to further develop CPLG’s cyber underwriting operation.

item.title: Reinsurance buyers expect further property rate declines: Moody’s
item.description: Reinsurance buyers expect property prices to continue declining into 2027, as abundant traditional reinsurance capacity and fewer severe catastrophe losses drive continued competition, according to Moody’s Ratings. Non-US insurers increasingly expect price declines, as abundant reinsurance capacity spills over from the property market. In its annual survey of reinsurance buyers, Moody’s noted that market conditions remain favourable for reinsurance buyers heading into 2027.

item.title: Starr names Liliane Wehbe as Head of Casualty, MENA
item.description: Starr, an insurance and investment organisation, has appointed Liliane Wehbe as Head of Casualty, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). In her new role, Wehbe will be based in Dubai and lead the development of the insurer’s regional specialty casualty offering, drive growth, and further broaden the solutions offered to clients and brokers. Most recently, she served as the Assistant Vice President and Head of Casualty at Liberty Specialty Markets for the past two years, also based in Dubai.

item.title: Amazon Sued by FTC Over Claims It Misled Advertisers on Pricing
item.description: over claims the e-commerce giant systematically overcharged advertisers for years. The FTC, which enforces antitrust and consumer laws, and the state attorneys general allege in the suit filed Monday that Amazon gave advertisers inadequate disclosures around the pricing and terms of the “sponsored” listings that users see as the top products when they search the company’s marketplace. “The FTC claims advertisers were harmed because they didn’t understand how our auction worked and therefore overpaid,” Amazon said in an emailed statement.

item.title: Thailand Shifts Disaster Risk to Insurers With $467 Million Plan
item.description: Thailand plans to provide government-funded disaster insurance to about 30 million households in high-risk areas, while seeking to shift some of the growing cost of floods and other catastrophes to private insurers. Thailand currently spends at least 30 billion baht a year compensating households for disaster losses, according to government estimates. Under the plan, insurers would take responsibility for payouts beyond the limits covered directly by the government, potentially reducing the taxpayers’ cost of major catastrophes.

item.title: Two Oil Supertankers Hit by Projectiles in Hormuz, Marisks Says
item.description: Two oil supertankers were struck by unknown projectiles in quick succession while transiting the Persian Gulf’s Strait of Hormuz chokepoint, maritime security consultant Marisks said. Earlier, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said that one tanker reported being struck by three unknown projectiles while completing an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz. The Senegal Prosperity, operated by Sinokor, was struck by three projectiles while traveling east of the same country, it said.

item.title: Texas, Louisiana Under Tropical Storm Warning as System Grows
item.description: Tropical storm warnings have been issued for parts of the Texas and Louisiana coast as a potential system gathers strength in the Gulf of Mexico. Any intensification will likely be short-lived, however, with the system forecast to move inland Tuesday, bringing heavy rain and a risk of flooding to parts of Texas and Louisiana. The still-unnamed storm was 130 miles (209 kilometers) south of Morgan City, Louisiana, with top winds of 35 miles per hour, the US National Hurricane Center said in an advisory on Monday.

item.title: Bamboo Files for IPO
item.description: (Image credit: Angelo Giordano/Pixabay.) Bamboo Insurance (Midvale, Utah) has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. The company has applied to list its Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol BMB, according to a Bamboo statement. Bamboo says the proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus.

item.title: Aon Acquires USI Insurance From KKR for $17 Billion
item.description: Related: Aon Acquires USI Insurance From KKR in $17 Billion Deal Targeting Middle Market After years of dealmaking doldrums, the recent boom in mergers and acquisitions is helping buyout shops sell more of their private equity bets and return cash to shareholders. is set to reap a $3.3 billion windfall from its deal to sell USI Insurance Services to Aon Plc for $17 billion, a significant exit for a unit that’s invested its balance sheet in long-term private equity bets. The transaction will generate about $2 billion of adjusted net income for the private equity giant, according to a statement.

item.title: Sony, Warner Music Sue Anthropic Over Songs Used in AI Training
item.description: Sony and Warner also said Anthropic used their lyrics to teach Claude to “generate vast quantities of purportedly ‘new’ AI-generated song lyrics, which compete with Music Publishers’ legitimate copyrighted works as harmful market substitutes.” The labels are seeking damages of up to $150,000 for each infringed copyright and a court order barring Anthropic from using their works. The music publishing branches of Sony Music and Warner Music have sued Anthropic in California federal court for allegedly misusing their copyrighted song compositions to train its Claude AI models. Sony and Warner said in the complaint, filed on Friday, that Anthropic pirated hundreds of song lyrics and sheet music from The Beatles, Taylor Swift, Michael Jackson and hundreds of other artists to train Claude to respond to human prompts.

Officials struggled for years to curb high-speed crashes along a residential corridor cutting through Albuquerque, New Mexico, but simply punishing the lead-footed drivers didn’t seem to work.

item.title: Produce Supplier Taylor Farms Often Failed to Disclose Workplace Injury Tallies: Report
item.description: Over the past five years, five to seven Taylor Farms facilities filed the annual report within the following year, with some showing injury rates above industry averages, while others recording below-average rates. Taylor Farms, the produce company at the center of a U.S. cyclospora outbreak, frequently failed to submit federally required workplace injury logs in recent years, including for at least four facilities where workers suffered fatal or otherwise serious injuries, a Reuters review of federal records found.

item.title: California Lawmakers File Wildfire Plan, Without Newsom Asks
item.description: California legislators introduced a bill Saturday that would update the state’s wildfire response without shifting liability away from publicly traded utilities. Lawmakers snubbed Newsom’s push to bar insurance companies from suing utilities for wildfire-related claims through a process known as subrogation. The legislation is the result of a compromise with Newsom and is intended to bolster the state’s wildfire recovery response amid a rapidly warming climate.

item.title: Sentry’s Dairyland to Return $30 Million to Florida Auto Insureds
item.description: Auto insurer Dairyland announced that it will return $30 million in savings to eligible Florida private passenger automobile policyholders through a one-time dividend. “Recent reforms have helped create a fairer market environment for everyone, and we’re committed to sharing the benefits of those improvements with Florida drivers while helping them manage the cost of their auto insurance.” said Pete Anhalt, president of personal lines at Sentry, Dairyland’s parent company. In addition to the one-time dividend, Dairyland recently lowered its Florida auto insurance rates by an average of 14%.

item.title: American Airlines to Pay $200K for Discrimination Against Worker With Blindness
item.description: American Airlines will pay $200,000 to settle a disability discrimination lawsuit brought by the U.S. According to the EEOC’S lawsuit, American Airlines failed to provide a reasonable accommodation to an employee at its Fort Worth location after she developed cortical blindness. The lawsuit charged American Airlines with failing to take legally required steps to enable the employee to use the screen reader software for her job or help her find another reasonable accommodation, instead keeping her on unpaid, involuntary leave for almost four years and then firing her after failing to facilitate her return to work.

item.title: AM Best Downgrades Financial Rating of Illinois’ Prime Insurance
item.description: AM Best has downgraded the Financial Strength Rating to B (Fair) from A- (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating to “bb+” (Fair) from “a-” (Excellent) of Prime Insurance Company based in Chicago, Illinois. The ratings will remain under review pending the filings of Prime’s statutory financial statements for third-quarter 2026, and AM Best’s meeting with management to better assess the company’s reserves, risk-adjusted capital and any and/or all mitigation tactics available. The ratings of Prime reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as adequate, as well as its adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and marginal enterprise risk management (ERM).

item.title: How Convective Storms Are Changing Insurance
item.description: Severe convective storms often produce remarkably uneven damage, and those sharp variations complicate nearly every stage of the insurance lifecycle. Unlike hurricanes that leave broad swaths of destruction, or floods that generally follow predictable topography, severe convective storms — including tornadoes, hail, damaging straight-line winds, and severe thunderstorms — produce highly localized, rapidly evolving damage that defies broad assumptions. As severe convective storms become an increasingly persistent source of insured losses, competitive advantage will depend less on understanding regional weather patterns and more on translating property-level weather intelligence into faster decisions, smarter claims handling, and stronger customer trust.

item.title: USI alleges former transportation leader moved clients to ECBM
item.description: USI Insurance Services has sued ECBM and former USI producer Robert Anderson, alleging that Anderson violated post-employment restrictions by moving two transportation accounts to his new brokerage. The complaint, filed July 9 in Erie County, New York, says Anderson left USI in June 2025 after serving as a producer and transportation team leader. USI alleges that he later joined ECBM and solicited, diverted or accepted business from CaraVan Inc.

item.title: Insureon partners with LIO Insurance
item.description: Insureon announced a partnership with specialty commercial property and casualty carrier LIO Insurance. The partnership expands Insureon’s ability to connect small business owners with specialized insurance solutions for niche risks. Insureon shares our focus on making commercial insurance simpler and more accessible.
